title: Revit MCP server Claude AI automation
summary: Understand Claude and Revit MCP automation, version requirements, local connections, and ArchiLabs Desktop as an integrated frontier AI alternative.
body_markdown:
A Revit MCP server can connect an AI client such as Claude to tools that inspect or change a live BIM model. The appeal is clear: explain the task in project language and let the assistant use application tools to help carry it out. The quality of the result depends on the complete setup, including the model, the server's actual capabilities, the source information, and the user's understanding of the intended deliverable.


This guide explains the architecture and the buying decision. For teams that want frontier intelligence and a broader working environment already brought together, ArchiLabs Desktop is our recommended alternative.


## Revit MCP server Claude AI automation


There are three main parts to this workflow. Claude is the AI client in which the user describes the assignment. The MCP server exposes tools the client can request. A Revit integration makes the supported operations available in the application and model.


MCP is the connection standard. It does not define a universal list of Revit capabilities, guarantee that a particular operation is supported, or make every server compatible with every Revit release. The server you choose determines the actual tools and version requirements.


Autodesk's public documentation describes its Revit MCP Server as a Technical Preview used with external AI clients such as Claude Desktop. Its documented uses include model queries, element information, navigation, and supported tasks.[Autodesk Revit Public MCP documentation](https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/2027/ENU/Revit-GetStarted/files/GUID-80B05F4F-1642-46BD-ACED-699D3125AEB9.htm) .


## Revit versions change the connection decision


Autodesk's preview announcement identifies Revit 2027.2 and later as the supported environment for its public-server previews. A team on Revit 2024, 2025, or 2026 therefore needs to evaluate a different, explicitly compatible connection rather than assuming the Autodesk package will work.[Autodesk's preview announcement and version guidance](https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/revit-architecture-forum/mcp-server-for-revit-tech-preview-launch/td-p/14262009) .


For a community server, inspect the release assets, version matrix, installation instructions, and maintenance history. A statement that code should work on an older version is weaker evidence than a release built and documented for that version. Keep the Revit build and connector release together in the office's setup record.


This is also an operational choice. Identify who will support the setup when a package changes, a workstation is replaced, or a project remains on an older Revit release. A connection that works for one technically confident user is not automatically a supported workflow for the entire office.


## Read tools and write tools answer different questions


A read operation can identify elements or return parameter values. A write operation changes the project. These should be evaluated separately, even when they appear in the same conversational interface.


Autodesk's preview announcement distinguishes Read-Tools, Trusted-Write, and Experimental packages. Those names describe different scopes; a demonstration of one does not establish the capabilities of another.[Review the package distinctions](https://forums.autodesk.com/t5/revit-architecture-forum/mcp-server-for-revit-tech-preview-launch/td-p/14262009) .


Begin with a task whose answer can be checked in the model. Ask for a defined set of elements and inspect the returned identity and values. Then evaluate a narrowly scoped supported change on a project copy, with a clear expectation for which objects should change and which should remain as they are.


For a schedule correction, the useful result is the correct model data and resulting schedule. For a documentation task, inspect the actual views and sheets. The conversation helps coordinate the work; the native result establishes what happened.


## Local and remote MCP connections are different setups


Claude documents both local server mechanisms and remote connectors. A remote connector is reached from Anthropic's infrastructure, while local server configuration is a separate mechanism. The supported surface and installation path matter, so follow the current instructions for the exact Claude experience you intend to use.[Claude's remote connector guidance](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-get-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp) and[local server guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/10949351-getting-started-with-local-mcp-servers-on-claude-desktop) .


A local Revit connection also does not, by itself, establish that all AI processing stays on the workstation. The server location, model service, transmitted tool results, and account terms are separate considerations. An office should understand that data path before selecting a production workflow.


Avoid copying a configuration from an unrelated server simply because both use MCP. The executable, transport, environment, and tool behavior belong to the chosen implementation. Good setup documentation explains why each part exists and what a successful connection looks like.


## Frontier intelligence needs useful project context


The most interesting tasks begin outside the model. A specification changes, a workbook arrives, or a coordination image shows a problem. The assistant needs that evidence and a clear statement of the intended result before a model operation becomes useful.


A good brief identifies the authoritative source, the objects or views involved, the relevant project convention, and the expected deliverable. When the evidence conflicts, make the decision explicit. The benefit of capable reasoning is helping the team work through that situation, not merely choosing a tool name from a list.


That is why the surrounding workspace belongs in the comparison. Consider how the user supplies visual context, manages files, inspects activity, and retains useful instructions. These everyday interactions often determine whether an office keeps using an AI workflow after the initial experiment.


## ArchiLabs Desktop: a Revit MCP alternative for the whole assignment


ArchiLabs Desktop brings frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic, reasoning-effort controls, native Revit and AutoCAD work, rich inputs, and editable knowledge into one product experience. The user starts with the project task and its evidence.


Desktop accepts PDFs and Excel workbooks, supports annotated captures and PDFs, lets users narrate screen recordings, and captures native selections. Native capabilities include modeling, families, routing, schedules, tags, dimensions, and sheets. Its public equipment recording shows a manufacturer PDF becoming a native Revit family and then being placed in a project. See[Desktop in action](https://archilabs.ai/desktop) .


Personal, project, team, and company knowledge libraries preserve the conventions that should apply again. Entries support editing, supporting files, and revision history. Connected accounts can supply additional authorized project context, while files and activity remain accessible in the working conversation.


This combination makes ArchiLabs compelling for teams that want the broader environment ready around their CAD/BIM work. A standalone MCP setup may suit an office that wants to assemble its own client and tools; Desktop is our first recommendation when the priority is useful delegation across a changing project workload.


## Choose a setup you can keep useful


Match the connection to the installed Revit release, confirm the actual read and write tools, and evaluate a representative deliverable. Include preparation, troubleshooting, corrections, review, and maintenance in the comparison.
